whatItIs.heading: What is ceiling water damage?
whatItIs.body: Ceiling water damage occurs when moisture infiltrates from above — whether from a roof leak, second-floor plumbing failure, HVAC condensate line backup, or a bathroom pan overflow. The ceiling is almost never the origin point. Drywall absorbs water fast and loses structural integrity faster: a saturated ceiling panel can sag within hours and collapse within days. Beyond the collapse risk, trapped moisture between the drywall and the subfloor above creates ideal mold conditions within 24 to 48 hours. Proper remediation requires identifying the source, stopping active intrusion, removing saturated material, drying the structural cavity, and restoring the finished surface — in that order. Skipping straight to paint covers the stain but leaves moisture in the wall cavity.

process.heading: How we handle ceiling water damage

steps.title: Source identification and safety check
steps.body: We use thermal imaging cameras and calibrated moisture meters to map the wet zone and trace it back to the origin — roof deck, supply line, condensate drain, or bathroom above. If the ceiling is actively sagging, we assess collapse risk before anyone works beneath it.

steps.title: Controlled opening, extraction, and drying
steps.body: We cut precise inspection openings to access the cavity, extract standing moisture, and deploy high-capacity air movers and dehumidifiers targeted at the structural assembly. Moisture readings are logged daily until the cavity reaches dry standard — not estimated, measured.

steps.title: Reconstruction and finish
steps.body: Once the structure is dry and any mold threat is cleared, we close the openings, texture-match the drywall, and restore the ceiling to pre-loss condition. One crew handles it start to finish — no handoff gap between mitigation and repair.

signs.heading: Signs you need ceiling water damage service now
signs.intro: Any one of these warrants a same-day call. Two or more is an emergency.

items.title: Visible stain or discoloration
items.body: A yellow-brown ring or spreading dark patch means moisture has already reached the drywall paper. The saturation underneath is typically three to five times the size of the visible stain.

items.title: Sagging or bubbling drywall
items.body: A ceiling that bows downward is holding water weight. This is a collapse warning — keep the area below clear and call immediately.

items.title: Active drip
items.body: If water is dripping through, the cavity above is already saturated. The drip is overflow, not the full volume of water present.

items.title: Musty smell with no visible damage
items.body: Moisture trapped inside a ceiling cavity produces a mildew odor before any stain appears. By the time you smell it, mold growth may already have started.

items.title: Peeling paint after a rain event or upstairs incident
items.body: Paint peeling from a ceiling — especially in patterns that follow joist lines — indicates the paper face of the drywall is wet and the bond has failed.

whyUs.body: Most contractors handle either mitigation or reconstruction — not both. pricing.heading: Ceiling water damage repair costs
pricing.body: Ceiling water damage repair in Southern California typically runs $600 to $4,500. A small localized stain with no structural involvement sits at the lower end. Costs rise with ceiling area affected, the complexity of reaching and repairing the source (a second-floor supply line is different from a condensate line), extent of mold growth, and whether full drywall replacement and texture matching are required. The range is wide because the source matters as much as the ceiling itself. Gallagher Restoration provides a free on-site assessment — we won't quote over the phone because an accurate number requires a moisture meter and a look above the surface. If the damage is covered by your homeowner's policy, we coordinate directly with your insurance adjuster and document the claim on your behalf.

faqs.q: Can I just paint over the water stain and skip the repair?
faqs.a: No. Paint over a water stain seals the surface but leaves moisture in the drywall and the cavity above it. That moisture continues to promote mold growth and drywall degradation. Within weeks, the stain typically bleeds through the new paint — and the underlying damage is now worse. The only permanent fix is drying the cavity to measurable dry standard before any finishing work.

faqs.q: How do you find where the water is actually coming from?
faqs.a: We use thermal imaging cameras and calibrated moisture meters to detect temperature differentials and saturation levels inside the ceiling assembly without unnecessary demolition. Most source identification requires one or two small inspection cuts rather than opening the entire ceiling. We map the wet zone and work backward to the origin.

faqs.q: How long does ceiling water damage drying take?
faqs.a: Drying a ceiling cavity typically takes 3 to 5 days under professional equipment — air movers, dehumidifiers, and daily moisture readings. Thicker assemblies or heavy saturation can extend that to 7 days. We don't remove equipment based on time — we remove it when the moisture readings confirm the material has reached dry standard.

faqs.q: Will my homeowner's insurance cover ceiling water damage?
faqs.a: It depends on the cause. Sudden and accidental events — a pipe burst, an appliance failure, an HVAC overflow — are typically covered. Gradual leaks that developed over time are often excluded. Gallagher Restoration documents the damage and works directly with your adjuster. We won't give you a coverage opinion, but we'll give your insurer everything they need to make one.
